chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu al-Husayn al-Nakha'i from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I was standing in prayer, and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was sitting in front of me, and I did not know him. Then 'Ibad al-Basri came to him. He said, so he offered the greeting of peace, then sat down and said to him: O Abu al-Hasan, what do you say about a man who performed Tamattu' and did not have a sacrificial animal (hady)? He said: 'He fasts the days that Allah, the Exalted, said.'
So I began to listen closely to the two of them. 'Ibad said to him: And which days are they? He said: 'The day before al-Tarwiyah, the day of al-Tarwiyah, and the day of 'Arafah.'
He said: If he missed those, he said: 'He fasts the morning of al-Hasbah and two days after that.'
He said: Do you not say as 'Abdullah ibn al-Hasan said? He said: 'What did he say?' He said: He said: 'He fasts the days of al-Tashriq.'
He said: 'Indeed Ja'far used to say: Indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Budayl to proclaim: 'These are days of eating and drinking, so let no one fast.'
He said: O Abu al-Hasan, indeed Allah said: 'So fasting three days during the Hajj and seven when you return.'
He said: 'Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The entire month of Dhu al-Hijjah is from the months of Hajj.'

And whoever fasts the day of al-Tarwiyah and the day of 'Arafah, then he fasts one other day after the days of al-Tashriq. And if he did not fast the day of al-Tarwiyah, it is not permissible for him to fast 'Arafah, but it is obligatory upon him to fast three consecutive days after the completion of the days of al-Tashriq.
That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The day of Arafah (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the fasting rules for a Hajj pilgrim who did not sacrifice an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of Kaffarah (expiation) for the Tamattu' pilgrim lacking a sacrifice, highlighting the scholarly nuance between Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq’s view that Dhu al-Hijjah is entirely part of the Hajj months and the Prophet’s prohibition of fasting during the Days of Tashriq. It establishes a precise chronological sequence for fasting—prior to, during, or after the Hajj days—depending on which days were missed, thereby resolving potential conflicts between Quranic verses and Prophetic traditions regarding fasting during pilgrimage.
